headline: Bitcoin ETFs flip negative for 2026 after $1.28B outflow week as Treasury moves against MEXC
summary: A brutal week for Bitcoin ETFs — $1.28 billion in net outflows erased all 2026 inflows — pushed the Fear & Greed Index to 28, deep into fear territory. The broader market barely moved in price terms, but the institutional selling pressure and a Treasury action targeting offshore exchange MEXC set a distinctly risk-off tone. The day's real story is structural: the smart money that piled into BTC ETFs earlier this year is now heading for the exits, and regulators are tightening the screws on exchanges operating outside U.S. oversight.

winners.name: Figure Heloc
winners.catalyst: Figure Heloc's tokenized HELOC product (a home-equity line of credit packaged as a blockchain token) gained 4.25% as traders rotated toward yield-bearing real-world asset tokens while Bitcoin ETF outflows weighed on speculative positions. No specific news catalyst was identified.

losers.name: Bitcoin Cash
losers.catalyst: Bitcoin Cash fell 4.78%, pressured by the broader risk-off sentiment following the $1.28 billion Bitcoin ETF outflow week and a Fear & Greed Index of 28. No BCH-specific catalyst was identified.

whyItMoved:
The headline number today isn't a price — it's $1.28 billion. That's how much left Bitcoin ETFs over the past week, the worst outflow stretch since June and enough to wipe out every dollar of net inflows recorded in 2026. The Fear & Greed Index sitting at 28 ("Fear") reflects the mood: institutional buyers who drove the ETF boom earlier this year are now net sellers, and retail sentiment has followed.

Bitcoin itself barely moved — up just 0.07% to $75,887 — which is almost more unsettling than a sharp drop. The price is holding, but the underlying demand picture has deteriorated. Ethereum dipped 0.12% to $2,236.92. Most of the top 15 tracked assets moved less than 1% in either direction, a sign of a market in a holding pattern rather than active selling.

The one notable exception was Figure Heloc, up 4.25%, as traders rotated toward tokenized real-world assets — products that generate yield from things like home-equity loans — while speculative positions in large-cap crypto faced redemption pressure.

On the regulatory front, the U.S. Treasury moved to cut off MEXC, an offshore exchange accused of facilitating $16 billion in alleged illicit flows. Actions like this — targeting the pipes that connect global crypto trading to the U.S. financial system — have historically tightened liquidity conditions for assets that rely on offshore venues for price discovery.
worthKnowing: Binance's CFO stepped down nine days after a reported $6 billion hack; management says the departure was planned six months in advance, but the timing has raised governance questions about the world's largest crypto exchange.

Binance is closing accounts for users in several European countries by year-end, requiring them to withdraw assets before new fees take effect — part of an accelerating regulatory retreat from the EU.

A security breach at Gnosis Pay exposed card numbers, home addresses, and linked crypto wallet data, a reminder that crypto-connected payment products carry the same custodial risks as traditional fintech.
